maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune branches only during dormant season (before April 1) to prevent fungal Oak Wilt transmission ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide deep watering every 2–3 weeks during the first two summers until established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave fallen oak leaves in mulch rings under the canopy to shelter overwintering pupae and insulate tree root zone ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Protect young sapling trunks with wire tree guards or wraps to prevent winter deer buck rub and rodent gnawing ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot; do not divide or transplant once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Fragrant midsummer blossoms attract native bumblebees, hoverflies, and beneficial predatory parasitoid wasps ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/black_cohosh.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Celastrina-neglectamajor), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/black_cohosh.htm)

advisor_description: A dioecious multi-stemmed deciduous shrub (6–10 ft) with toothed dark green ovate leaves, producing dense clusters of bright red berry-like drupes on female plants that persist on bare branches through winter ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)). Requires a male pollinator nearby and grows in moist, acidic to neutral soils, rain gardens, and wetland margins ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/winterberry.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune in late winter or early spring before new growth starts; avoid heavy pruning that removes flower buds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture during dry periods ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Protect berry clusters from premature netting if holiday harvest is desired ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Plant containerized male and female plants within 50 feet ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Henry's Elfin butterfly (*Callophrys henrici*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callophrys-henrici)); small flowers attract native sweat bees and honeybees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Berries soften after winter freezes to feed Eastern Bluebirds, American Robins, Hermit Thrushes, and Cedar Waxwings ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/winterberry.htm)).

advisor_description: A low-growing rhizomatous perennial iris (4–8 in) with sword-shaped leaves, bearing lavender-blue flowers with crested white and orange ridges on the falls in April ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)). Spreads via surface rhizomes to form colonies in moist, well-drained, organically rich soils in partial to full shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Rake off heavy smothering leaves in early spring to expose emerging flower buds ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide partial shade and well-drained, organic-rich soil; drought tolerant once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide shallow rhizomes every 3–4 years immediately after spring flowering completes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Early spring blooms provide essential nectar for queen bumblebees and native long-tongued bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Hummingbirds frequently visit the early spring blooms; rhizomes are resistant to deer browsing ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Hummingbirds frequently visit the early spring blooms; rhizomes are resistant to deer browsing ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).

advisor_description: An upright herbaceous perennial (2–4 ft) with lanceolate leaves, producing erect terminal racemes of tubular scarlet flowers from July to September ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)). Grows in wet to moist soils in full sun to partial shade, suited for rain gardens, bioswales, stream banks, and shaded borders ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping, cane thinning, or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Gently clear fallen leaves from around basal rosettes in spring to prevent crown smothering ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistently moist to wet soils; do not allow root zone to dry out completely in summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave seed stalks standing so fine seeds can scatter onto moist surrounding soil to replenish colony ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Ensure basal winter rosettes receive light; do not bury under heavy layers of woodchips ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide basal rosette offshoots in early spring every 2–3 years to maintain long-term vigor ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Primary nectar source for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Archilochus-colubris)); flowers visited by large swallowtail butterflies.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Specially co-evolved floral structure transfers pollen onto the heads of foraging hummingbirds ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)).

wildlife_ecological_value:
**Host Plant Value:** Primary nectar source for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Archilochus-colubris)); flowers visited by large swallowtail butterflies.

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Specially co-evolved floral structure transfers pollen onto the heads of foraging hummingbirds ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Archilochus-colubris), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)

advisor_description: A stout, branched woodland perennial (3–5 ft) forming a large mound of bipinnately compound foliage, bearing spherical greenish-white umbels in midsummer followed by dark purple berry clusters in autumn ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276593)). Grows in moist, humus-rich woodland soils in partial to full shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276593)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures exceed 50°F before clearing away old dead stalks ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave ornamental milkweed pods to mature and disperse silken seeds naturally ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot; does not like root disturbance; propagate from fresh seed ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276864)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Feathery seedheads are collected by small birds for nest lining ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/prairie_smoke.html)).

Develops a rounded crown in average to moist, well-drained soils in full sun to partial shade, dropping foliage early in dry late summers ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/red_buckeye.html)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Water during hot summer droughts to reduce early foliage dormancy or leaf drop ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281049)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Collect fallen smooth buckeyes or leave for wildlife dispersal ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

advisor_description: An upright, branched perennial milkweed (3–5 ft) with lanceolate leaves, bearing flat-topped umbels of fragrant rose-pink flowers from July to August followed by erect, spindle-shaped seed pods ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276790)). Possesses fibrous roots adapted to wet to moist loams, heavy clay, rain gardens, and wetland margins in full sun ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/sw_milkweed.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back dead stems to 8–18 inches in late spring at 50°F+ (emerges late in May) ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture during severe summer droughts ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276790)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave slender upright seed pods to crack open and release silky seeds into autumn breezes ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Premier obligate host plant for Monarch caterpillars (*Danaus plexippus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Danaus-plexippus)); flowers attract swallowtails and native bees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Vanilla-fragrant nectar feeds dozens of butterfly species; silk from seed pods is used by goldfinches to line nests ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/sw_milkweed.htm)).

advisor_description: A small clumping perennial in the iris family (6–12 in) with narrow, sword-like linear leaves, producing 6-tepaled violet-blue flowers with yellow centers on flattened branched stems from May to June ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281168)). Grows in moist, well-drained loams and sandy soils in full sun to partial shade, self-seeding moderately in border margins ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/sbe_grassx.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back woody dead stalks to 3 inches in late spring at 50°F+; spade perimeter roots to contain aggressive clonal spread ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Chelsea chop: cut stems back by half in early June to promote sturdy, compact branching and prevent flopping ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277437)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave golden seedheads intact through winter for goldfinches and winter songbirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide expanding rhizomatous clumps every 2–3 years in early spring and spade boundaries to contain spread ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277437)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Keystone host for Silvery Checkerspot (*Chlosyne nycteis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Chlosyne-nycteis)), Painted Lady (*Vanessa cardui*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Vanessa-cardui)), and specialist bees (*Melissodes agilis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Melissodes-agilis)). Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Heavy seed yields provide crucial high-fat winter nutrition for goldfinches, nuthatches, and chickadees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277437)).

advisor_description: A tall perennial composite (4–8 ft) featuring large, leathery, cordate basal leaves (up to 2 ft long), sending up tall, nearly leafless scapes topped with yellow sunflower-like heads in late summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277363)). Develops a taproot reaching over 10 feet deep, enduring extreme drought in heavy clay and prairie soils in full sun ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/pr_dockx.htm)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temps consistently exceed 50°F before trimming away tattered overwintered leaves at the crown ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Apply 1–2 inches of light mulch around root crowns in late November to prevent frost heaving ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286873)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide mature woody crowns every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286873)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Prune out 3-year-old wood immediately after spring bloom to stimulate productive young canes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during fruit swell in midsummer; highly drought tolerant thereafter ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide rooted suckers in early spring or take dormant hardwood cuttings ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Sweet berries feed Catbirds, Brown Thrashers, Robins, and small native mammals ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Perform any structural pruning in late winter (January–February) while fully dormant to prevent beetle transmission of oak wilt ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide supplemental deep watering during severe drought in first 2 years of establishment ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Allow leaf litter to decompose under canopy to nourish soil mycelium and shelter overwintering pupae ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Protect young trunk base with wire cages to prevent winter rodent and deer damage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep root network; do not divide or transplant once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).

maintenance_guide.fall: Leave papery triangular seed capsules to self-sow naturally or collect for propagation ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Midsummer flower umbels attract numerous small sweat bees, mining bees, and hairstreak butterflies. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Onion scent naturally repels deer, rabbits, and voles, protecting companion plants ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282058)).

advisor_description: A low-growing perennial warm-season bunchgrass (8–15 in) with narrow basal foliage, producing horizontal, comb-like purplish seed heads held at right angles at the tip of slender stems in midsummer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=242377)). Spreads slowly by root suckers to form colonial thickets in moist, rich bottomland soils and woodland understories ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/pawpaw.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping, cane thinning, or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune unwanted root suckers in early spring to maintain a single-stemmed tree form rather than a colonial thicket ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=275970)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Maintain consistent soil moisture during midsummer fruit swell ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=275970)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest ripe pawpaw fruits in September as they soften and emit a tropical mango-banana scent ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Taprooted; propagate via fresh stratified seed or dormant sucker excavation; do not divide mature trees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=275970)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Sole obligate larval host for the Zebra Swallowtail butterfly (*Eurytides marcellus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/neographium-marcellus)) and the Pawpaw Sphinx moth (*Dolba hyloeus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Dolba-hyloeus)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Fallen fruits provide rich nutritional forage for opossums, raccoons, gray foxes, and woodland mammals ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/pawpaw.htm)).

advisor_description: A low-growing, succulent perennial groundcover (3–6 in) with rounded, fleshy leaves arranged in whorls of three, producing terminal 3-branched cymes of 4-petaled white starry flowers in spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279473)). Grows in moist, humus-rich woodland loams in partial shade, self-seeding moderately ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/wild_geranium.htm)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Late-summer nectar source for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds and migrating swallowtail butterflies ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/gb_lobeliax.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/gb_lobeliax.htm)

advisor_description: A colonial woodland perennial (1–1.5 ft) featuring paired, umbrella-like palmately lobed leaves, bearing a solitary nodding white flower in the fork of the stem in April, followed by a fleshy edible yellow fruit in summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277777)). Spreads by extensive subterranean rhizomes to form large colonies in moist, rich deciduous woodland soils in partial to full shade, entering dormancy in midsummer ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/mayapple.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back old flowering stems in early spring at 50°F+; spade perimeter to contain creeping rhizomes ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Deadhead spent flower umbels in midsummer to prevent aggressive self-seeding and promote a second wave of late-summer blooms ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277129)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide spreading rhizome clumps every 1–2 years in early spring or autumn to maintain garden boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277129)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Painted Lady butterfly (*Vanessa cardui*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Vanessa-cardui)) and various geometer moths.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Broad flat umbels are a premier landing platform for beneficial predatory parasitoid wasps and hoverflies ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277129)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Vanessa-cardui), [Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277129)

maintenance_guide.spring: Clean away collapsed foliage in early spring at 50°F+ as sky-blue flower bells appear ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide partial to full shade and moderate moisture to prevent summer dormancy ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285442)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Emerges late in spring (May); cut dead winter vines to the ground at 50°F+ and guide vigorous new shoots onto trellis ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Regularly pull and excavate wandering root runner suckers emerging outside designated garden boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284891)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest ripe yellow-green maypop fruits in September–October as they soften ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide spreading root runners in early spring while dormant or install root barrier collars to contain garden borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284891)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Sole obligate larval host for the Gulf Fritillary (*Dione vanillae*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Dione-vanillae)) and primary host for the Variegated Fritillary (*Euptoieta claudia*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Euptoieta-claudia)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Rake off heavy autumn leaves; shear back to 2–3 inches in early spring (50°F+) to refresh carpet before new growth ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Early-maturing seed achenes provide critical spring nutrition for ground-foraging woodland birds like Eastern Towhees and Wood Thrushes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279721)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune out dead, crossing, or diseased twigs immediately after spring flowering completes to maintain an open vase structure ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280440)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during extended summer droughts to prevent leaf scorch and verticillium stress ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280440)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave hanging seed pods on branches to provide late-season food for songbirds and gamebirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot; do not divide or transplant mature specimens ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280440)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Henry's Elfin butterfly (*Callophrys henrici*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callophrys-henrici)) and Redbud Leaf-folder (*Fascista cercerisella*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Fascista-cercerisella)); early spring flowers are crucial nectar for queen bumblebees (*Bombus*) and mining bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds are consumed by Northern Bobwhite, Tufted Titmice, Chickadees, and Cardinal species ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/redbud.htm)).

advisor_description: A stiffly erect, rhizomatous perennial (1.5–2.5 ft) with opposite, palmately 3-lobed leaves, producing terminal solitary yellow composite flower heads (up to 2 in across) in June and July ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277598)). maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back dead stems to the ground in spring after 50°F+ temperatures; spade perimeter to contain rhizomatous expansion ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Pull wandering perimeter shoots to maintain allocated garden space ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277598)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave seedheads intact to feed overwintering prairie songbirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide rhizome colonies every 2–3 years in early spring and spade edge to contain boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277598)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Wavy-lined Emerald Moth; specialist native bees (*Melissodes coreopsis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Melissodes-coreopsis)) feed heavily on pollen.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds provide high-energy nutrition for American Goldfinches, Field Sparrows, and Bobwhite Quail ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/pr_coreopsisx.htm)).

advisor_description: A deciduous medium tree (20–40 ft) with palmately compound 5-foliate leaves, bearing erect 4–7 inch panicles of yellow-green flowers in spring followed by spiny, leathery husks containing smooth brown seeds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281045)). Grows in moist, fertile woodland soils along river valleys and bluffs ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/oh_buckeye.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Provide afternoon shade or moist soil to minimize mid-summer leaf scorch ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281045)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Allow fallen buckeyes to decompose or feed native squirrels ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Early spring flowers attract native bumblebees, mason bees, and early butterflies; host for buckeye leaf miner. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Squirrels bury and feed on mature nuts; unpalatable to deer and rabbits ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/oh_buckeye.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during first 2 years; exceptional drought and heat tolerance once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278961)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave fruit clusters on branches to feed migrating thrushes and robins ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Plant containerized shrubs ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278961)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Spring Azure (*Celastrina ladon*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Celastrina-ladon)) and Clearwing Moths (*Hemaris thysbe*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Hemaris-thysbe)); flowers attract dozens of native pollinator species.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Black fruits (resembling raisins) are high in nutrition and feed Cedar Waxwings, Bluebirds, Northern Cardinals, and red foxes ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/blackhaw.htm)).

advisor_description: A clump-forming perennial composite (2–3 ft) with ovate basal leaves, producing abundant flower heads with bright golden-yellow ray florets and dark brown conical centers from July through October ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277460)). Spreads slowly via short rhizomes and self-seeding in average to moist, well-drained garden soils and rain garden margins in full sun to partial shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277460)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures consistently exceed 50°F before cutting dead stalks to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during severe drought; highly disease-resistant and reliable ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277460)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave dark cones standing through winter to feed goldfinches and chickadees ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous root clumps every 3–4 years in early spring to maintain vigorous flowering ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277460)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Silvery Checkerspot butterfly (*Chlosyne nycteis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Chlosyne-nycteis)) and Wavy-lined Emerald Moth.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Cones are a primary winter seed staple for American Goldfinches, Black-capped Chickadees, and Tufted Titmice ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277460)).

advisor_description: A sprawling, low-growing perennial (6–12 in tall, trailing 1.5–2 ft) with lanceolate leaves, producing large, 4-petaled canary-yellow flowers (up to 4 in across) that open in late afternoon from May to July, followed by broad winged seed capsules ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283032)). Develops a deep woody taproot adapted to dry, shallow, rocky limestone soils and glades in full sun ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283032)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back dried foliage to 2–3 inches in early spring once temperatures exceed 50°F before new green shoots emerge ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave standing foliage and seedheads undisturbed through fall and winter to feed winter sparrows and insulate the crown ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Slow-growing clump; division is rarely needed. If rejuvenating, divide large mature clumps in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285254)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Leonard's Skipper (*Hesperia leonardus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Hesperia-leonardus)), Cobweb Skipper (*Hesperia metea*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Hesperia-metea)), and Ottoe Skipper (*Hesperia ottoe*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Hesperia-ottoe)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds feed winter songbirds including Field Sparrows, Dark-eyed Juncos, and American Tree Sparrows; bunching base shelters overwintering bumblebees ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/pr_dropseed.htm)).

advisor_description: A deciduous suckering shrub (3–5 ft) with elliptic dark green leaves that turn deep scarlet-crimson in late autumn, bearing arching 3–6 inch cylindrical racemes of fragrant white flowers in early summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286893)). Spreads by root suckers to form colonies in moist to wet soils in full sun to shade, suitable for rain gardens and stream borders ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/va_swspire.html)).

advisor_description: A low stoloniferous perennial (6–12 in) forming basal rosettes of pubescent, spoon-shaped leaves, producing daisy-like composite flower heads with pale lavender-to-white ray florets and yellow centers in April and May atop hairy stems ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277317)). maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Shear back stems to 2–3 inches in early spring at 50°F+; spade edge bed boundaries deeply to sever spreading underground runners ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Shear back by half after main spring bloom wave to stimulate fresh compact foliage and deadhead spent seed capsules ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283036)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide shallow spreading runners in early spring or install physical underground root barriers to contain boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283036)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for White-lined Sphinx Moth (*Hyles lineata*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Hyles-lineata)) and specialist evening primrose sweat bees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Day-and-night opening flowers feed both diurnal native bees and nocturnal sphinx moths ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/sh_primrosex.htm)).

Prefers cool, moist, acidic, humus-rich soils in partial shade to dappled sun ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/al_dogwood.htm)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until sustained 50°F+ temperatures before cutting back dead winter stems to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Chelsea chop: pinch back stems by 1/3 in early June to promote dense branching and compact form ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=290710)).

**Host Plant Value:** Larval host for Wild Indigo Duskywing (*Erynnis baptisiae*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Erynnis-baptisiae)), Frosted Elfin (*Callophrys irus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callophrys-irus)), and Hoary Edge (*Achalarus lyciades*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Achalarus-lyciades)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Blooms are heavily visited by queen bumblebees (*Bombus*); seedpods shelter small native beneficial insects ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/bl_indigox.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Erynnis-baptisiae), [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callophrys-irus), [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Achalarus-lyciades), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/bl_indigox.htm)

advisor_description: An upright perennial herb (2–3 ft) with broad ovate leaves marked with chevron variegation, producing slender, wiry racemes (up to 12 in) of tiny white flowers from July to September followed by hooked achenes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291626)). Spreads via rhizomes and self-seeding in moist, organically rich deciduous woodland soils in partial to full shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291626)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back old dead stalks in spring after 50°F+ temperatures ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture and partial to full shade; highly pest-free ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291626)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave slender seed spires intact; seeds 'jump' when touched to self-sow in matrix gaps ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous root clumps in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291626)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Bronze Copper butterfly (*Lycaena hyllus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Lycaena-hyllus)) and various native geometer moths.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Small achenes provide late-autumn food for woodland gamebirds and native sparrows ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=291626)).

advisor_description: A branching, fibrous-rooted perennial (1.5–2.5 ft) with fern-like compound foliage, bearing nodding bell-like flowers with red sepals, yellow petals, and upward-projecting red nectar spurs in April and May ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286069)). Grows in well-drained, dry to medium rocky woodland soils, limestone slopes, and open borders in full sun to full shade, self-seeding freely ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/wild_columbine.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Clear old debris gently in spring (50°F+) as delicate ferny foliage emerges ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Cut stems back to basal foliage after flowering if columbine leaf miners tatter leaves ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286069)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave upright 5-lobed seed capsules to release glossy black seeds into surrounding matrix ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Short-lived perennial that self-sows freely; do not divide. Propagate via seed ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286069)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Columbine Duskywing (*Erynnis lucilius*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Erynnis-lucilius)) and visited by queen bumblebees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Long nectar spurs are tailored specifically for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*) ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/wild_columbine.htm)).

advisor_description: A semi-evergreen, mat-forming perennial (8–14 in) with opposite elliptic leaves, producing loose cymes of fragrant, 5-lobed pale blue to lavender flowers in April and May atop erect flowering stems ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285428)). Spreads by decumbent creeping sterile stems that root at nodes in moist, organically rich, well-drained woodland loams in partial to full shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285428)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Fragrant spring blooms provide crucial nectar for early-emerging bumblebees and hummingbirds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285428)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures consistently exceed 50°F before cutting dead stalks to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave rigid cones standing undisturbed through winter to feed goldfinches and native birds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune out root suckers deeply at the base in late winter or early spring to prevent colonial thicket expansion in garden borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286355)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Mow or spade emerging root suckers in adjacent lawn or garden beds; provide supplemental deep watering during prolonged droughts to swell fruit ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286355)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Collect fallen plums or leave for ground-foraging wildlife ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Excavate rooted suckers in late winter while dormant for propagation or disposal ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286355)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Host for Tiger Swallowtail (*Papilio glaucus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papilio-glaucus)), Red-spotted Purple, Cecropia Moth, and specialist bees including *Andrena pruni*. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Plums are eagerly sought by wild turkeys, foxes, raccoons, and songbirds; dense thorny branches provide impenetrable nesting cover ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_plum.htm)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papilio-glaucus), [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_plum.htm)

Forms dense upright clumps in average to dry soils in full sun, functioning as a primary component of tallgrass prairie restorations ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285219)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Emerges late in spring (May); cut back old stems at 50°F+ and spade bed edges deeply to sever and contain spreading rhizomes ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture; pull wandering surface runners to prevent crowding adjacent perennials ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277501)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide spreading rhizomes in early spring or pull perimeter runners annually to maintain strict bed boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277501)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Three-lined Flower Moth (*Schinia trifascia*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Schinia-trifascia)) and visited by hundreds of migrating Monarchs.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Unrivaled high-volume nectar source for migrating Monarchs, swallowtails, and native solitary bees in late fall ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/mistflower.htm)).

advisor_description: A short-lived perennial herb (1–1.5 ft) with sticky-pubescent stems and spatulate basal leaves, producing loose cymes of brilliant scarlet, 5-petaled flowers with deeply notched petals from May to July ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279088)). Grows in dry, rocky, well-drained open woodland soils, bluffs, and slopes in partial shade to full sun ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/firepink.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Requires partial shade and excellent drainage; avoid heavy wet clay around the crown ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279088)).
maintenance_guide.division: Short-lived perennial that self-sows naturally; do not divide. Propagate via fresh seed ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279088)).

advisor_description: An arching rhizomatous woodland perennial (1.5–3 ft) with alternating elliptic leaves along gracefully curving unbranched stems, bearing paired, bell-shaped greenish-white flowers dangling beneath leaf axils in May, followed by blue-black berries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281983)). Spreads slowly via thick knobby rhizomes in moist, humus-rich woodland soils in partial to full shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281983)).

maintenance_guide.fall: Leave blue-black berries on arching stems for woodland birds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Dangling bell blossoms are pollinated by queen bumblebees (*Bombus*) and long-tongued solitary bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Blue-black autumn berries provide nourishment for Wood Thrushes, Veeries, and small native rodents ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281983)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Blue-black autumn berries provide nourishment for Wood Thrushes, Veeries, and small native rodents ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281983)).

advisor_description: A rhizomatous perennial woodland grass (2–3 ft) with bamboo-like lanceolate leaves, bearing drooping terminal panicles of flattened, chevron-shaped spikelets that turn bronze-copper in autumn ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285270)). Spreads via short rhizomes and self-seeding in moist, rich soils in partial shade to full sun, suitable for shade gardens, bioswales, and erosion control ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285270)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back to 2 inches in spring after sustained 50°F+ temperatures; pull dense emerging self-sown seedlings from garden mulch ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Deadhead drooping seedheads in late summer if preventing prolific self-seeding throughout garden beds is desired ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285270)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave decorative seed clusters on stems for winter movement and wildlife forage only if prepared to weed spring seedlings ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide dense fibrous clumps in early spring or pull unwanted self-sown seedlings ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285270)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Northern Pearly-Eye (*Enodia anthedon*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Enodia-anthedon)), Pepper and Salt Skipper, and Bell's Roadside-Skipper.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Heavy dangling seeds are a staple winter food for Cardinals, Juncos, and small mammals ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285270)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds provide high-energy nutrition for American Goldfinches, Field Sparrows, and Bobwhite Quail ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/sand_coreopsisx.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Vanessa-cardui), [Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277194)

advisor_description: A deciduous understory tree (15–25 ft) with spreading horizontal branches, bearing 4 large white petal-like bracts surrounding tiny green flowers in early spring, followed by bright red berries and scarlet autumn foliage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279338)). Performs best in moist, organically rich, well-drained acidic soils in partial shade ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/flw_dogwood.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping, cane thinning, or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune dead wood in late winter while dormant; avoid pruning in late spring when borer beetles are active ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279338)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water deeply every 10–14 days during dry summer spells to prevent anthracnose and mildew stress ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279338)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave red fruit clusters for songbirds; allow leaves to decompose under drip line ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Plant ball-and-burlap or containerized trees with root flare exposed ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279338)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Spring Azure (*Celastrina ladon*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Celastrina-ladon)) and Io Moth (*Automeris io*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Automeris-io)); early spring flowers provide nectar for mining bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Bright red drupes are a primary high-energy food for 36+ bird species including Eastern Bluebirds, Wood Thrushes, and Cardinals ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/flw_dogwood.htm)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Cut stems back to 12–18 inches in early spring (at 50°F+) as flowers bloom on current season growth ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Propagate via stratified seed or layering ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=295801)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Feathery seed clusters are collected by songbirds for soft nest insulation ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=295801)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures exceed 50°F before cutting dead stalks to 8–18 inches; spade edges to restrict expanding colony width ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Chelsea chop: pinch stems back by 1/3 in early June to promote dense bushy growth, and thin dense center stems to improve air circulation ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281404)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave aromatic button seedheads intact through winter to feed native songbirds, or deadhead if limiting self-seeding is preferred ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous rhizomatous clumps every 2–3 years in early spring to contain perimeter spread and discard woody centers ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281404)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Hermit Sphinx (*Lintneria eremitus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Lintneria-eremitus)) and Gray Marvel (*Phobolosia anfracta*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Phobolosia-anfracta)); magnetic nectar source for clearwing sphinx moths.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: High-sugar tubular flowers are heavily favored by Ruby-throated Hummingbirds and long-tongued bumblebees (*Bombus pensylvanicus*) ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/wld_bergamotx.htm)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Lintneria-eremitus), [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Phobolosia-anfracta), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/wld_bergamotx.htm)

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until sustained 50°F+ temperatures before cutting back dead winter stems to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave golden-bronze seedheads intact through fall and winter to feed songbirds and shelter beneficial insects ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous root clumps every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277364)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Keystone host supporting 100+ caterpillar species and specialist mining bees (*Andrena asteris*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Andrena-asteris)). Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Essential late-season nectar feast for woodland butterflies; seeds sustain chickadees and juncos all winter ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/zz_goldenrod.htm)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Andrena-asteris), [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/zz_goldenrod.htm)

advisor_description: A long-lived deciduous conifer (50–70 ft) featuring feathery needle-like foliage that turns copper-bronze in autumn before shedding, fibrous reddish-brown bark, and conical form ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=m510)). Highly adapted to saturated soils and standing water where it produces root 'knees', but also grows vigorously in normal upland garden clay ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/bald_cypress.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune dead or competing central leaders in late winter before soft needle emergence ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=m510)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide deep watering during first 2 years; completely flood-proof and surprisingly drought-hardy once rooted ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=m510)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Allow fallen needles to create an acid-buffering, weed-suppressing natural mulch ring ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Plant containerized or ball-and-burlap specimens ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=m510)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Bald Cypress Sphinx Moth (*Isoparce cupressi*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Isoparce-cupressi)) and various microlepidoptera.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Wood Ducks and migratory water birds feed on cone seeds; massive branching provides eagle and osprey nesting roosts ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/bald_cypress.htm)).

advisor_description: A deciduous rhizomatous fern (2–4 ft) forming upright vase-shaped rosettes of feathery, bright green sterile fronds, accompanied by separate rigid, woody, dark brown fertile fronds that persist through winter ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285874)). Spreads by underground stolons to form colonies in moist, fertile, organically rich soils in partial to full shade ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/ostrich_fern.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: High Maintenance in garden settings. Spreads aggressively via vigorous running rhizomes, root suckers, or prolific self-seeding. Requires active seasonal management (annual boundary spading, root-barrier containment, or deadheading) to prevent overtaking beds and displacing companion perennials.
maintenance_guide.spring: Harvest tight curled fiddleheads as a spring delicacy or allow them to unfurl; clear away dead previous-year fronds at 50°F+ ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture in shade; spade perimeter runners to prevent spreading colonies from crowding smaller shade companions ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285874)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide and sever creeping rhizome runners every 2–3 years in early spring while dormant to contain colony spread ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285874)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Ostrich Fern Borer Moth (*Papaipema speciosissima*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papaipema-speciosissima)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Stately frond colonies provide sheltered foraging grounds for Wood Thrushes and American Toads ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/ostrich_fern.htm)).

advisor_description: A loose, open deciduous shrub (4–6 ft) with coarse, fuzzy ovate leaves, bearing tiny pinkish-white flowers in summer followed by dense, tight clusters of iridescent violet-purple drupes encircling the stems in autumn ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)). Grows in average to moist, well-drained soils in full sun to light shade, dying back to the ground in severe winters ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut stems back to 12–18 inches in late winter (50°F+) to encourage dense new fruiting wood ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide moderate moisture in full sun to part shade; highly drought-resilient once rooted ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Protect berry clusters from early pruning so songbirds can feed into winter ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Propagate via softwood cuttings in summer or seeds in autumn ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Rustic Sphinx (*Manduca rustica*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Manduca-rustica)); summer blossoms buzz with long-tongued native bees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Over 40 species of songbirds devour the purple berries, including Northern Mockingbirds, Cardinals, and Brown Thrashers ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Prune branches only in summer after full leaf emergence to prevent excessive sap bleeding ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Deep soak every 2–3 weeks during the first two summers of establishment ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taprooted legume; do not divide. Plant containerized saplings into well-drained loams ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Hanging legume pods feed Northern Bobwhite and small woodland rodents in late winter ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/yl_wood.html)).

advisor_description: An erect, clumping perennial herb (1–2 ft) with opposite ovate leaves, producing one-sided terminal cymes of tubular scarlet-red flowers that flare open at the apex into a 5-pointed yellow star in June ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282481)). Grows in moist, well-drained, organically rich soils in partial shade, establishing a non-invasive long-lived clump ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/indian_pink.html)).

advisor_description: An upright perennial composite (2–3 ft) with narrow lanceolate foliage and hairy stems, bearing flower heads with drooping, slender pinkish-purple ray florets and yellow pollen around a spiky central cone in June and July ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277423)). Possesses a deep taproot adapted to dry, calcareous glades, rocky hillsides, and borders in full sun ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277423)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures exceed 50°F before cutting dead stalks to the crown ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave spiky dark cones standing through winter to feed American Goldfinches ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Cones are a premier winter seed staple for American Goldfinches, Chickadees, and Juncos ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277423)).

Forms non-aggressive bushy clumps in dry to moist soils, woodland borders, and prairie restorations in full sun to partial shade ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/dwn_skullcap.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut stems back to the ground in spring after 50°F+ temperatures ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave cup-shaped seed capsules resembling miniature helmets for native seed dispersal ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous clumps every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281520)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Hooded blue blossoms attract bumblebees, long-tongued solitary bees, and beeflies. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Foliage contains bitter skullcap compounds that naturally deter deer and rabbit browsing ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/dwn_skullcap.htm)).

wildlife_ecological_value:

advisor_description: A multi-stemmed deciduous shrub (5–12 ft) with pinnately compound foliage, bearing broad flat cymes (up to 10 in) of fragrant white flowers in early summer followed by heavy clusters of dark purple-black berries in late summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)). Spreads by root suckers to form loose thickets in moist to wet soils along riparian edges, ditches, and sunny margins ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).
