maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping, cane thinning, or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back weak, dead, or 3-year-old stems to the ground in early spring (50°F+) to stimulate vigorous fruiting canes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture during fruit development; spade emerging unwanted suckers to maintain bounds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest berries for culinary use or leave for songbird migration fuel ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide spreading root suckers in early spring or take hardwood cuttings ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for the Elderberry Borer Beetle (*Desmocerus palliatus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Desmocerus-palliatus)) and Cecropia Moth; hollow pithy stems are premier nest sites for solitary bees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Over 50 species of birds eagerly consume elderberries, including Gray Catbirds, Brown Thrashers, Cardinals, and Bluebirds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Desmocerus-palliatus), [Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Over 50 species of birds eagerly consume elderberries, including Gray Catbirds, Brown Thrashers, Cardinals, and Bluebirds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).

advisor_description: A multi-stemmed deciduous shrub (8–12 ft) with broad ovate leaves turning copper-bronze in autumn, male catkins opening in early spring, and edible round nuts enclosed in ragged leaf-like husks in late summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277820)). Spreads by root suckers to form dense thickets in average to moist soils in full sun to partial shade ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_hazelnut.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Thin out oldest canes in late winter to stimulate vigorous young nut-bearing wood ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277820)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during first 2 years; exceptional drought tolerance and adaptability to heavy clay ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277820)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest hazelnuts in August–September before wildlife claims them ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide spreading root suckers in early spring while dormant ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277820)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Polyphemus Moth (*Antheraea polyphemus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Antheraea-polyphemus)), Io Moth, and Hazelnut Weevil.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Hazelnuts are a premier high-fat wildlife staple for Wild Turkeys, Blue Jays, Ruffed Grouse, and chipmunks ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_hazelnut.htm)).

wildlife_ecological_value:
**Host Plant Value:** Larval host for Polyphemus Moth (*Antheraea polyphemus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Antheraea-polyphemus)), Io Moth, and Hazelnut Weevil.

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Hazelnuts are a premier high-fat wildlife staple for Wild Turkeys, Blue Jays, Ruffed Grouse, and chipmunks ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_hazelnut.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Antheraea-polyphemus), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_hazelnut.htm)

advisor_description: A dioecious deciduous small tree or large shrub (12–20 ft) bearing drooping 4–8 inch panicles of fragrant white, strap-like petals in late spring before leaves fully expand, with female plants producing dark blue olive-like drupes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282950)). Grows slowly in moist, fertile, acidic soils in full sun to partial shade ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/fringetree.html)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Water during extended summer droughts; adapts readily to both moist rich soils and heavy urban clay ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282950)).

Spreads via above-ground stolons to colonize dry, poor, rocky or gravelly soils in full sun, withstanding severe drought ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=302490)).

Spreads by submerged creeping rhizomes and starchy overwintering tubers in saturated mud and shallow standing water in full sun ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cm_arrowhead.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping, cane thinning, or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until sustained 50°F+ temperatures before cutting dead stalks to the crown ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water at soil level during severe drought to prevent powdery mildew stress; provide good air circulation ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285435)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave seed capsules for winter bird foraging ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous root crowns every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285435)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for the Phlox Moth (*Schinia indiana*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Schinia-indiana)) and visited by tiger swallowtails and clearwing moths.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Deep tubular flowers provide abundant nectar for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds and large butterfly species ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/sm_phlox.htm)).

advisor_description: A semi-evergreen, mat-forming perennial (8–14 in) with rounded, toothed basal rosettes, producing branched corymbs of bright yellow daisy-like composite flowers in April and May atop erect stems ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=292089)). Spreads via stolons to form groundcovers in dry to moist rocky woodland soils, slopes, and borders in partial shade to full sun ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/rl_ragwort.html)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Rake away smothering tree leaves in early spring at 50°F+; semi-evergreen rosettes awaken quickly ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Highly drought-tolerant once established in shade; suppresses weeds throughout summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=292089)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Foliage contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids that make it completely immune to deer and rabbit browsing ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/rl_ragwort.html)).

advisor_description: A bushy, clump-forming perennial mint (2–3 ft) with finely textured, needle-like aromatic leaves, producing dense flat-topped terminal clusters of small white flowers with purple speckles from July to September ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281417)). Spreads slowly via short rhizomes in dry to moist soils and heavy clay in full sun, without invasive behavior ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/slm_mintx.htm)).

advisor_description: A rhizomatous wetland perennial iris (2–3 ft) with slender, arching green leaves, producing flat, drooping copper-to-red flowers in May and June atop slender branched stems ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281153)). Spreads by shallow rhizomes in moist to wet saturated soils, shallow standing water, and rain garden basins in full sun to partial shade ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/copper_iris.html)).

advisor_description: A cool-season perennial bunchgrass (1–2 ft) forming dense tufts of narrow, bluish-gray basal leaves, producing silvery-green cylindrical spike-like panicles from May to June that mature to golden-tan ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285326)). Grows in well-drained, dry to medium sandy or rocky soils in full sun, with high drought tolerance ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/june_grass.htm)).

advisor_description: A tall perennial warm-season bunchgrass (4–7 ft) with blue-green stems and basal leaves turning reddish-bronze in autumn, bearing 3-parted 'turkey-foot' digitate racemes from August to October ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285262)). Possesses extensive roots extending over 10 feet deep, adapted to average to moist loams and heavy clay in full sun ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285262)).
